analysis.title: The Off-Balance Sheet Time Bomb Inside AI Hits $4.1 Trillion: Up $1 Trillion In 90 Days
key_insights: Disclosed off-balance sheet commitments across the hyperscalers, Nvidia, Broadcom and SpaceX are $4.11 trillion, built from primary filings. That is up $992 billion from Morgan Stanley's $3.12 trillion filings-only tally, or $4.29 trillion including the news-based items MS also showed.
The author's tally was $1.8 trillion in June and $3.1 trillion in August, so the total rose about $1 trillion in roughly 90 days.

Alphabet is the first company with more than $1 trillion of off-balance sheet commitments at $1,059 billion, up from $890 billion in the MS chart. Its long-term purchase commitments rose from $707 billion to $802 billion.

Meta is at $866 billion and growing faster than Alphabet. Signed but not yet commenced leases total $1.39 trillion, up from $1.12 trillion in August. Purchase commitments are $2.25 trillion, up from $1.73 trillion. Guarantees and backstops rose from $158 billion to $273 billion.
The five companies that have filed Q3 10-Qs saw combined off-balance sheet commitments rise from $2.48 trillion to $3.05 trillion in Q3, up $577 billion or 23%.

Meta rose $195 billion (+29%). Non-cancelable purchase commitments went from $349 billion to $455 billion, leases not yet commenced from $279 billion to $356 billion, including $68 billion of leases signed in July. Residual value guarantees on its two data center ventures are $41.5 billion.
Meta's CDS hit a record after earnings. The company then went to shareholders for an equity raise, with a roughly $60 billion ATM program to follow.

Amazon rose $131 billion (+41%). Unconditional purchase obligations went from $130 billion to $254 billion, with a new $159.6 billion property and equipment row. Leases not yet commenced rose from $137 billion to $165 billion. Amazon fell Friday after a capex shock.

Alphabet rose $164 billion (+18%). Purchase commitments rose $95 billion, leases not yet commenced went from $85 billion to $131 billion, and energy equipment guarantees went from $7.6 billion to $16.2 billion. There is a new $6.6 billion line of guarantees to repurchase TPU hardware. Alphabet has already raised $80 billion in equity.

Microsoft rose $35 billion (+6%). It signed about $53 billion of new data center leases in Q3, partly offset by $17 billion that commenced. Leases not yet commenced went from $329 billion to $365 billion. Its $229 billion of purchase commitments is still as of June because it discloses them only in the 10-K, and Microsoft recently needed $25 billion in bonds.

SpaceX rose $51 billion (+174%), from $29 billion at June 30 to $40 billion in its 10-Q, then to $80 billion after a $40 billion Apollo GPU master finance lease disclosed in an 8-K on October 26 (schedules commencing in 1H27).
Nvidia, Oracle and Broadcom have not reported Q3 yet and are still on summer filings. Nvidia reports in late November and Oracle and Broadcom in December, so the author calls $4.1 trillion a floor.

Goldman credit strategist Amanda Lynam puts hyperscaler off-balance sheet exposures (leases and purchase commitments) at $2.8 trillion across five hyperscalers, an eightfold increase since 2023. Hyperscalers remain low-levered and highly rated.
Rating agencies treat these exposures inconsistently. S&P adjusts leverage for off-balance-sheet leases while Moody's and Fitch do not, so methodology changes are worth watching.
The author counts $3.3 trillion across Alphabet, Meta, Microsoft, Amazon and Oracle alone, including guarantees and backstops.

On-balance sheet debt and lease liabilities across the eight companies total roughly $1.0 trillion, so there are more than four dollars of off-balance sheet commitments per dollar reported. Needham argued Meta is 35% more expensive once off-balance sheet debt is added to enterprise value.

Nasdaq 100 members have wiped out more than $1.2 trillion of market cap this month, and Alphabet suffered a record plunge. The author says AI became the largest sector in the investment grade market last October.

market_movers.rationale: Off-balance sheet commitments of $1,059 billion are the largest of any hyperscaler, and free cash flow keeps going deeper in the red. The stock had a record plunge.

Commitments of $866 billion are growing faster than Alphabet's. CDS hit a record after earnings and the company is raising equity. Needham says it is 35% more expensive on an EV basis including off-balance sheet debt.
Commitments rose 41% in Q3, the largest percentage jump among hyperscalers, and the stock fell Friday after a capex shock.
Described as the cleanest hyperscaler, but its $229 billion of purchase commitments is stale (as of June) and likely higher when updated. It recently needed $25 billion in bonds.

sector_views.rationale: The AI buildout runs on debt and an increasing share is off balance sheet, with the Nasdaq 100 losing more than $1.2 trillion of market cap this month.

earnings_insights: Alphabet, Meta, Microsoft, Amazon and SpaceX have filed Q3 10-Qs. Nvidia reports in late November, and Oracle and Broadcom in December.
Amazon fell Friday after a capex shock following its Q3 report.
Meta's CDS hit a record after its Q3 earnings, followed by an equity raise.
risk_factors: Morgan Stanley warns that if supply and demand normalize ahead of expectations, companies may have to pay for excess capacity or renegotiate terms.
Hyperscaler free cash flow is going deeper in the red while commitments grow.
The funding window may narrow with each quarter as commitments grow and equity and bond raises increase.
Rating agency methodology changes could alter how the leases are treated.
Counterparties on much of the purchase commitments are unnamed, and the circular financing structure among AI companies adds opacity.
vol_and_positioning: Meta CDS hit a record after earnings.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscalers remain low-levered and highly rated per Goldman's Lynam. Morgan Stanley says the commitments are strategically important while supply remains constrained.
tension_points.bear_case: Off-balance sheet commitments are more than four times reported debt and leases and are growing about $1 trillion a quarter, while free cash flow weakens and equity raises begin.
tension_points.what_invalidates: If supply and demand normalize ahead of expectations, companies may have to pay for excess capacity or renegotiate terms (Morgan Stanley). Revenue would need to catch up before the next trillion is signed.

theme_stances.key_argument: The AI buildout runs on debt and a growing share is off the books, and the liabilities come due regardless of the stock price.
